description:
[narrowed from a-cutover-commits-another-gaps-staged-edit-under-its-own-attribution] A compose cutover for one gap committed another gap's staged edit under its own attribution, and mirrored only its own files — leaving the swept-in change present in git and absent from the running tree.

OBSERVED 2026-09-10 11:11:17. An operator dispatch edited repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/patch-with-tools.ts, adding a diagnostic to the semantic gate's PASSED log line. It reached origin/dev inside commit 2a5a305, whose message is "substrate-authored: apply recommit-ten-of-eleven-rhythm-families-have-no-staleness-driver-syntax_break-compose-report via mitosis cutover" — a completely unrelated gap about rhythm staleness drivers. `git log -S` confirms 2a5a305 is the commit that introduced the line; the operator's own dispatch produced no commit of its own.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS, BOTH FOLLOWING FROM THE SAME CAUSE.

  1. MIS-ATTRIBUTED LANDING. The commit says it applies the rhythm-families gap and
     in fact carries an unrelated change to the patcher's logging. Anyone asking
     "what did this gap change?" — an operator, a closure predicate, the gap store's
     own durability accounting, a future bisect — gets a wrong answer. Worse, the
     compose that owns the commit never judged the change it carried: the semantic
     gate that ran, ran against the rhythm-families patch.

  2. GIT AHEAD OF RUNTIME. The cutover mirrored its own staged files to /vessels and
     not the swept-in one. Measured immediately after: origin/dev contains the line,
     /vessels/development-vessel/src/resolvers/patch-with-tools.ts does not, and the
     vessel restarted at 11:11:36 — after the 11:11:17 commit — so the restart did
     not carry it either. The runtime is behind git for that file until the next
     pull-sync reconciles it.

THIS IS THE CONCURRENT-COMPOSE CLASS IN THE LANDING DIRECTION. The same root cause is
already recorded on the refusal side: "SKIPPING ROLLBACK ... file content has changed
(likely by another concurrent compose)", where a refused compose's bytes survive
because another compose touched the file. Here the same shared-tree contention runs
forward instead of backward: whichever compose reaches cutover first commits whatever
is in the tree, including work it did not author and did not gate.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. Every accounting this substrate keeps about its own
self-modification is attribution-based — which gap closed, which compose landed, which
lane authored what. Commit attribution is the substrate's ONLY durable record of that,
and it is wrong whenever two composes overlap on one vessel. It also silently defeats
the one-operation-per-plan discipline that the partial-landing evidence recommends: a
plan can be atomic and still arrive inside someone else's commit.

VERIFY BEHAVIOURALLY. Dispatch two edits to different files in the same vessel so their
composes overlap, then check that each resulting commit contains only the ops of the
gap it names, and that /vessels matches origin/dev for every file the commit touched.
Reading the cutover source is not sufficient — the contention is a timing property.

CORRECTION — DEFECT 2 IS TRANSIENT, NOT A PERMANENT SPLIT. The entry above described the swept-in change as present in git and absent from the running tree, which was true at the moment of measurement and overstated as a standing condition. Watched to resolution: substrate-pull-sync reconciled it on its next tick.

    11:11:17  commit 2a5a305 lands, carrying the swept-in edit
    11:11:36  vessel restarts WITHOUT it (cutover mirrored only its own staged files)
    11:22:38  pull-sync: "development-vessel: content a9772a7943 -> c1290737f0
              (git 2a5a30567c) — mirroring", then "[mirror-to-live]
              development-vessel mirrored (2a5a305) -> /vessels"
    11:23:10  deployed = 1

So the runtime lags git by at most one pull-sync period — roughly ten minutes — and
then converges by content hash. That is a real window in which a committed change is
not running, and it is worth knowing when reasoning about "did the fix take effect
yet", but it is NOT a divergence that persists or requires intervention. The
content-addressed mirror is doing exactly the job it was hardened for.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. Mis-attribution does not self-heal.
Commit 2a5a305 will say "apply recommit-ten-of-eleven-rhythm-families..." forever
while containing an unrelated change to the patcher's logging, and no later tick
repairs a commit message. Every attribution-based question — which gap changed what,
which lane authored it, what a closure predicate should look for, what a bisect will
blame — stays permanently wrong for any commit produced while two composes overlapped
on one vessel. Judge the severity on that, not on the ten-minute mirror lag.

src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts(2217,5): error TS2448: Block-scoped variabl
- typecheck_dangling_reference: src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts(2208,63): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'modifiedByPatchTools'.
src/resolvers/vessel-mitosis-cutover.ts(2217,24): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'modifiedFiles
- compose_execution_failure: {"error":"no_unique_anchor: refused fs_edit — planned anchor is non-unique and re-derivation found no unique substring (would mislocalize to first occurrence)"}

Do not repeat these failures. Address the specific cause named above.
